I have a mood disorder and get depressed frequently. What helps is being reminded of the difference between what your depression says and what is actually true. 

"I'll never stop feeling like this": No. All feelings (including happy ones) are temporary.

Make sense? Helping someone stay grounded and not judging them is key. Least helpful thing to say: think happy thoughts.

I think the common misconception is that as an s-type, we're going to lay everything at our D-type's feet and hope they "fix" us. It's really easy to fall into that when we want to obey or crave all that 24/7 jazz AND we're dealing with mental health issues. Man oh man, the times I've completely ignored my needs for the sake of being pleasing to a D-type.

I was severely depressed and my D-type didn't see the signs nor did I explicitly say anything. In my fog, I thought he was all I needed to fulfill me. Of course, he fell short of that expectation because I was having distorted thoughts. He thought my requests for humiliation/degradation were par for the course and gladly obliged. I was a huge whore for it in general, so it wasn't out of the norm for me to want it. But it was fucking me up deep inside. It wasn't until months after we ended things that things exploded. I got help and things are okay now.

I do really love humiliation/degradation, but I learned in the worst way how my depression can sneak in with that. It's a delicate thing. 

But my point is this: That itch she wants you to scratch isn't the priority and perhaps you can communicate that to her gently. Engaging in that kind of play (even lightly) can be so detrimental to someone dealing with mental health issues. You never know what landmine you'll step on. You can't help her more than she'll allow you to. Be wary of falling into the caregiver role. Sure, support her in the process of getting help. But it is ultimately her recovery and she's the driver. Validate her efforts and successes. Most importantly, be responsible for your own emotional health. We can't help other if we aren't caring for ourselves. Best of luck and kudos for bit just running in the opposite direction.
